microtheory.name: epistemic_access
microtheory.definition: The 'I don't know for sure, but I know how to GET it' stance, and the decision of whether to ask now / bank for later / drop. Sits between low-weight conjecture and a categorical inadmissible 'I don't know': a resolvable gap carries an acquisition ROUTE (a person who'd know, an external reference, or a solved class) plus a COST. The surface-vs-bank decision is a cost-benefit over the CONVERSATION itself — value (materiality now) against social cost (social capital, flow disruption, face/imposition, cumulative question burden) — not a single confidence cutoff. Verified core: feeling-of-knowing (Koriat accessibility + cue-familiarity cascade), feeling-of-findability (dissociable external-locatability judgment), transactive memory (Wegner: who-knows-what, label+location not content), value-based seek control (CHOICE + PERSEVERANCE). Social-cost decision half + the solved-class judgment are standard pragmatics (Brown-Levinson face, Grice relevance/quantity, Clark common ground) flagged scaffolding (not verified in this pass). Composes with the confidence continuum from [[conjecture]]. Substrate analogue: the teacher/references are external stores; the discourse referents are interlocutor sources; a banked gap is a pending node resolved off the social path (the babble loop made deliberate).

concepts.name: epistemic_access_stance
concepts.definition: The per-query metacognitive verdict, extending the confidence continuum: GROUNDED (high) > order-N CHAIN (decaying) > CONJECTURE (epsilon shape-guess) > RESOLVABLE_VIA_ROUTE (don't know, but gettable via an acquisition_route at a cost) > INADMISSIBLE (not even gettable -> categorical 'I don't know'). The new band is resolvable_via_route: it converts a flat 'I don't know' into 'I don't know, but I can get it from <route>'.

concepts.name: feeling_of_knowing
concepts.definition: FOK: the heuristic sense that an answer is retrievable from one's OWN store WITHOUT having retrieved it. Not privileged access — inferred as a by-product of the retrieval attempt from the quantity of partial information surfaced (accessibility_heuristic), and it rises with partial-info quantity regardless of correctness (so it is fallible, a calibratable estimate not ground truth). Substrate analogue: how many partial matches / related concepts the grounded store surfaces for the query.

concepts.name: cue_familiarity_gate
concepts.definition: First stage of the FOK cascade (Koriat-Levy-Sadot): the familiarity of the QUERY/cue itself acts early and must clear a threshold to trigger interrogation of memory. Only when cue familiarity is high does the accessibility_heuristic get read out. Substrate analogue: is the query about concepts the agent holds at all (familiar terms) -> worth searching.

concepts.name: accessibility_heuristic
concepts.definition: Second stage of the FOK cascade: FOK scales with the amount of partial answer-information that becomes accessible during the retrieval attempt, read out only when cue_familiarity_gate has cleared. CONTESTED vs the cue-familiarity/preretrieval camp (Reder/Metcalfe/Schwartz); the settled synthesis is the DUAL cascade (familiarity first, accessibility second), so build both stages, not accessibility alone.

concepts.name: feeling_of_findability
concepts.definition: FOF: a SEPARATE, dissociable judgment of how easily/quickly a currently-unknown answer can be LOCATED in an EXTERNAL store, uncorrelated with FOK and predictively valid (predicted ease tracks actual ease). This is the 'I know how to get it' signal proper. Substrate analogue: is the query a kind a reference (Wiktionary/WordNet/teacher) or a known interlocutor can supply -> external gettability.

concepts.name: transactive_memory
concepts.definition: Wegner: a directory of WHO-KNOWS-WHAT (and where info lives), built from learning others' domains of expertise; a query routes by default to the acknowledged domain expert, letting one retrieve far beyond one's own store. Used as a ROUTING / distributed-access mechanism, NOT a literal group mind (the strong emergent-group-cognition reading is contested). Substrate analogue: a who-knows-what map over discourse referents + external stores.

concepts.name: knowing_where_vs_what
concepts.definition: Retrieval from ANY external store needs only two things beyond the item: a retrieval-cue/LABEL and a notion of its LOCATION — the content itself need not be held. Knowing WHERE an answer lives is a distinct, often more valuable capability than knowing WHAT it is. Grounds the resolvable_via_route stance: the agent can know the route without the answer.

concepts.name: acquisition_route
concepts.definition: A concrete way to obtain a missing answer, attached to a resolvable_via_route gap: (a) INTERLOCUTOR — a discourse entity who would know (transactive: typically the entity the question is about, or the current addressee); (b) REFERENCE — an external store (Wiktionary / WordNet / VerbNet / the teacher boundary ~ 'Wikipedia'); (c) SOLVED_CLASS — general confidence the question is of a lookupable/computable/has-an-authority kind even with no specific source. Each route carries a cost-to-obtain.

concepts.name: solved_class_judgment
concepts.definition: General confidence that a question belongs to a CLASS of problems with a known method/answer (lookupable, computable, or has an authority) even without a specific source in mind — so it is gettable in principle. SCAFFOLDING: requested but did NOT surface in the verified research; teach as a standard judgment to ground later (e.g. against the agent's reference coverage = which question-types its stores can answer).

concepts.name: value_based_seeking
concepts.definition: The seek-now-vs-defer decision is value-based cost-benefit control: seek/offload when the answer's expected value exceeds the cost. Internal retention carries an OPPORTUNITY cost (limited capacity, interference); external seek carries an effort/time cost. Monitoring outputs CAUSALLY drive this control (not epiphenomenal). The umbrella over choice_stage + perseverance_stage.

concepts.name: choice_stage
concepts.definition: Stage 1 of seek control: WHETHER to seek at all + in what order. Driven by judgments of learning — drop items believed already known (don't ask what you can answer), then prioritize by region-of-proximal-learning (the most learnable/material-not-yet-known first). Substrate analogue: only seek when grounded + chain + conjecture have failed AND the answer is material.

concepts.name: perseverance_stage
concepts.definition: Stage 2 of seek control: keep the current route vs SWITCH/abandon. Governed by the perceived RATE of progress (jROL, the derivative of online learning), not the static level: continue while progress is rapid ('on a roll'), switch/stop when progress approaches zero ('going nowhere'). jROL is heuristic and its veridicality is questioned — a calibratable signal. Substrate analogue: if a route isn't yielding, try another (interlocutor -> reference -> bank).

concepts.name: help_seeking_is_multifactor
concepts.definition: The decision to SURFACE a query to an interlocutor is NOT a single confidence cutoff. Confidence is only WEAKLY coupled to help-seeking (replicated x3) though strongly to WITHHOLDING — so asking is guided by a WIDER set: informativeness, time cost, independence (preference to solve alone), curiosity, audience appropriateness, AND (this project's emphasis) the social cost. Build the surface decision as multi-factor, not a threshold on confidence.

concepts.name: surface_vs_bank_vs_drop
concepts.definition: Given a resolvable_via_route gap, the control output: ASK-NOW (surface to this audience), BANK (defer — resolve later via another route, off the social path), or DROP (immaterial at this point). Decided by a cost-benefit over the conversation: surface iff the answer is material NOW and the value exceeds the social cost given the accumulated burden; else bank if another route exists; else drop. The deliberate form of the babble loop (ask only when worth it).

concepts.name: materiality
concepts.definition: Whether the answer is relevant/needed for the CURRENT goal or exchange ('is it immaterial at this point?'). The VALUE side of surface_vs_bank_vs_drop. An immaterial gap is dropped (or silently banked), never surfaced — connects to the agent's held Gricean relevance maxim. SCAFFOLDING: the relevance/materiality model is standard pragmatics (Grice), not verified in this pass.

concepts.name: social_capital
concepts.definition: A finite resource the agent SPENDS by asking questions; it depletes with each ask and regenerates slowly. A budget on the surface decision: even a material, route-having question may be banked if social_capital is low. Asking constant questions disrupts flow and depletes capital — the human discipline of not over-asking. SCAFFOLDING: conversational-economics framing, not verified in this pass.

concepts.name: conversational_flow_cost
concepts.definition: The disruption a question imposes on conversational coherence — an off-topic / interrupting question breaks flow. Part of the COST side of surface_vs_bank_vs_drop: a question that derails the current exchange costs more than one that fits. SCAFFOLDING: standard discourse-coherence framing, not verified in this pass.

concepts.name: face_imposition
concepts.definition: Brown-Levinson politeness theory: a question is a face-threatening act — it imposes on the addressee (demands their attention/effort, can threaten their or the asker's face). The imposition is part of the social COST of asking, and motivates hedging / indirectness when a question must be surfaced. SCAFFOLDING: politeness theory, not verified in this pass; connects to the agent's held pragmatics.

concepts.name: cumulative_question_burden
concepts.definition: The social cost of asking RISES with frequency: each recent question raises the cost of the next, so a run of questions becomes disruptive / annoying even if each is individually cheap. Implemented as the depletion term on social_capital. The reason a good conversational citizen banks most resolvable gaps rather than asking them all.

concepts.name: audience_appropriateness
concepts.definition: Whether THIS interlocutor is a plausible + appropriate source within the common ground — a precondition on surfacing (Clark audience design): ask the entity who plausibly knows (transactive routing) and only when it's within shared ground. An inappropriate audience -> bank/route elsewhere even if the gap is material. SCAFFOLDING: Clark common-ground/audience-design, no primary source verified in this pass.

concepts.name: bank_for_later
concepts.definition: A resolvable gap recorded as a PENDING node to resolve later via an acquisition_route OTHER than interrupting the current audience (the teacher boundary / a reference / a future turn with a better source). The deliberate, cost-managed form of the babble loop: acquire-and-ground cumulatively, off the critical social path, so the conversation isn't burdened. Resolved when the source becomes available.

concepts.name: monitoring_drives_control
concepts.definition: The metacognitive monitoring signals (FOK, FOF, confidence, jROL) CAUSALLY drive the control actions (seek / withhold / surface / bank), shown by experiments dissociating perceived from actual learning. Justifies wiring the gettability + confidence + route state directly into surface_vs_bank_vs_drop. Both help-seeking and withholding are triggered by low confidence; the wider multi-factor set then decides which.
